0.long_answer: Moyamoya disease type 2 is associated with mutations in the RNF213 gene. This gene, located on the long arm of chromosome 17 (specifically at 17q25.3), has been identified through linkage analyses as a significant susceptibility factor for the disease. Although the mutation in RNF213 contributes to the development of moyamoya, research suggests that this mutation alone may not be sufficient to cause the condition. Other genetic or environmental factors likely play a role in disease manifestation.
